paper.title: Learning Superconductivity from Ordered and Disordered Material Structures
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces SuperCon3D, a new dataset of experimental crystal structures (both ordered and disordered) paired with superconducting transition temperatures (Tc), and proposes two deep learning models: SODNet for Tc prediction and screening of known structures, and DiffCSP-SC for generative inverse design of novel high-Tc superconductors. It validates both models on benchmark tasks and reports candidate materials for experimental validation.

task.objective: predicting the Tc values given the crystal structure M. Then, we use the predicting models to screen the big structure database to find candidate superconductors with high Tc value.

evidence.text: Superconductivity Prediction Task. The task involves predicting the Tc values given the crystal structure M. Then, we use the predicting models to screen the big structure database to find candidate superconductors with high Tc value.

stages.stage_name_raw: extracting superconductors from SuperCon and ICSD
stages.stage_goal: collect superconducting materials with chemical formulas and critical temperatures
stage_output: 208,425 ordered and disordered crystal structures from ICSD

evidence.text: We extracted approximately 33,000 superconductors with their chemical formulas and corresponding critical temperatures from SuperCon. After removing duplicates and non-superconductors, we identified 11,949 superconducting materials. Additionally, over 200,000 ordered and disordered crystal structures were gathered from the ICSD database [3].

stages.stage_name_raw: matching SuperCon entries with ICSD entries
stages.stage_goal: match superconductor entries with crystal structures based on chemical composition, space group and lattice parameter
stage_output: 1,578 superconductor data entries, each featuring both Tc and crystal structure

evidence.text: We then matched these 11,949 SuperCon entries with 208,425 ICSD entries based on chemical composition, space group and lattice parameter.

stages.stage_name_raw: collating Tc values and structural data from literature
stages.stage_goal: obtain Tc values and structural data for hydrogen-enriched superconductors from literature sources
stage_output: Tc values and structural data for hydrogen-enriched superconductors

evidence.text: Moreover, Tc values and structural data for hydrogen-enriched superconductors were collated from various literature sources.

stages.stage_goal: train the SODNet model to predict Tc from crystal structures

evidence.text: Based on SuperCon3D, we propose two deep learning methods for designing high Tc superconductors. The first is SODNet, a novel equivariant graph attention model for screening known structures, which differs from existing models in incorporating both ordered and disordered geometric content.

stages.stage_name_raw: screening the ICSD database using SODNet
stages.stage_goal: identify potential high-Tc superconductors by applying SODNet to the entire ICSD database

evidence.text: Using our model, we screened the ICSD database to identify potential high-Tc superconductors. Appendix E.2 lists 27 candidates, including cuprate, H-rich, heavy-Fermion, iron-based, and other types.

stages.stage_name_raw: performing DFT calculations on selected candidates
stages.stage_goal: verify superconducting properties of generated candidates via density-functional theory

evidence.text: Subsequently, density-functional theory (DFT) were performed on selected candidates to verify their superconducting properties. Notably, Van Hove singularities (VHS) were observed in the electronic structures of Ba2CuCl2O2, Lu, and BaFe2Se2, as further detailed in Appendix E.5.
